simple.meaning: מֶרְחָב (merchâb) is a Hebrew action word meaning “enlargement , either literally (an open space , usually in a good sense), or figuratively ( liberty ).” BibleIQ anchors the English reading to this source verb before comparing its uses.
simple.biblicalBackground: This action appears 6 times in 2 Samuel, Psalms, Hosea, Habakkuk, beginning at 2 Samuel 22:20. The surrounding contexts include birth, righteousness, Israel.
simple.inThisVerse: In this verse, the tapped English word is source-aligned to מֶרְחָב (H4800) in the Hebrew text.
simple.whyItMatters: Actions in Scripture show what people do, what God does, and how covenant faithfulness or rebellion is described. BibleIQ compares the action across its occurrences.
simple.summary: מֶרְחָב (merchâb) / H4800 is traced through 2 Samuel 22:20, Psalms 18:20, Psalms 31:9, Psalms 118:5 with source-language evidence and verse context.

timeline.evidenceText: He also brought me out into a large place.
Yahweh has rewarded me according to my righteousness.
Have mercy on me, Yahweh, for I am in distress.
Out of my distress, I called on Yah.
For Israel has behaved extremely stubbornly, like a stubborn heifer.

For, behold,† “Behold”, from “הִנֵּה”, means look at, take notice, observe, see, or gaze at. It is often used as an interjection. I raise up the Chaldeans, that bitter and hasty nation, that march through the width of the earth, to possess dwelling places that are not theirs.
